title: Is ShipBob’s Technology Behind the Curve? A Look Inside the Full Fulfillment Stack
summary: See inside ShipBob's full fulfillment stack: owned end to end, with real-time analytics, AI that acts, and full control over every order.
body_markdown:
Store owners comparing fulfillment providers sometimes run into a few specific worries about ShipBob’s technology that cluster around three ideas: standardized processes can’t handle complex or specialized logistics, an outsourced model means less hands-on control, and the dashboard looks modern but the reporting and analytics fall short for serious data needs.


A few go further and call the technology outdated.


Fulfillment software is easy to judge from a demo and hard to judge from the outside, and providers in this category genuinely differ in how their technology is built. ShipBob has also shipped a lot of new capabilities quickly, so what someone saw a year or two ago may not match what the platform does today.


This guide explains where that impression comes from and shows how ShipBob’s fulfillment technology actually works today: what you can see, what you can control, and what the system can do on your behalf.


## Where the “behind the curve” impression comes from


Put simply, the worry is that ShipBob’s technology looks polished but can’t keep up once your operation gets complicated.


The assumptions behind it usually sound like this:


- Standardized fulfillment processes won’t suit complex or specialized logistics.
- An outsourced model means limited hands-on access to your inventory and orders.
- The dashboard is modern, but the deeper reporting and analytics are thin.
- Modern-looking is not the same as capable, so the technology may be behind the curve.


This is the misconception: that ShipBob’s platform is a clean interface sitting on top of shallow capability, fine for simple stores but not for brands with real operational complexity.


## The real test: does it change an operational outcome?


The real test of fulfillment technology isn’t how it looks in a 30-minute demo. A clean dashboard, a chatbot, and a few reports that render nicely are easy to build. Software that actually does the work is not.


A traditional 3PL gives you warehouse space and whatever software happens to run it.


**ShipBob is built the other way around, with the technology as the product and fulfillment running on top of it.**


That difference comes down to four things:


1. ShipBob built and owns every layer of the stack, on one codebase.
2. The analytics exist to run operations, not just to look at.
3. The AI acts on your account, it doesn’t only describe it.
4. You keep control, and a complete record of every action taken.


The rest of this guide takes each one in turn.


## A look at the full stack, point by point


Each point below pairs what it looks like in day-to-day operations with a brand that has put it to work.


### ShipBob built and owns the entire stack


ShipBob was founded by engineers who built and have owned the whole stack from day one: the[ShipBob WMS](https://www.shipbob.com/product/wms/) , the fulfillment engine, the transportation network engine, the merchant application, the API layer, and the network itself.


All of it runs on one codebase, which is why the platform behaves as one connected system for your entire operation, digital and physical.


You view your data, run operations, flag and swap SKUs, choose the carrier that delivers cost-effectively, and track shipments in real time, in one place.


Complexity is where that shows, for example:


- DTC, marketplace, and B2B or EDI-automated orders run from a shared inventory pool.
- Lot-controlled and temperature-sensitive products are handled with first-expired, first-out rotation.
- You can run a hybrid model, outsourcing in some regions while using ShipBob WMS in your own warehouse in others.


Providers that grew by renting or acquiring pieces of their technology have to connect those pieces after the fact, which leaves every site on a different system and every fix waiting on someone else’s roadmap.


#### Why technology ownership matters for store owners


- One system for global operations, not a set of disconnected tools
- Complex logistics handled in-house, from placement to carrier selection
- Faster fixes and new features, because the roadmap isn’t outsourced
- Consistent behavior across every location


**Proof:**[ZBiotics](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/zbiotics/) ships all of its inventory to a single hub and lets ShipBob’s[Inventory Placement Program](https://www.shipbob.com/product/inventory-placement/) distribute it across the network, even as it scaled production 15X.


> *“My favorite thing about the Inventory Placement Program is that it takes the burden off of our team and it’s based on real-time calculations, giving us the right distribution by SKU at each fulfillment center. It’s comforting to know that we have a good balance between fulfillment centers on a day-to-day, week-to-week, and month-to-month basis, so our customers receive packages via the lowest shipping zone possible among the four ShipBob fulfillment centers we’re in across the US.*
>
>
> *That ultimately helps us get products to our customers faster, giving them a great ZBiotics experience from start to finish.”*
>
>
> *Michael Mullaney, VP of Supply Chain at[ZBiotics](https://zbiotics.com/)*


### The analytics are built to run operations


In the ShipBob dashboard, you get:


- Real-time inventory across every location
- SKU velocity and estimated days of inventory left
- Average fulfillment cost per order
- Storage cost per unit
- Shipping-method performance


Fulfillment SLA and exceptions reporting is there too, and the reports export to CSV so your team can work with the data in its own tools.


ShipBob also publishes its own network performance publicly and updates it weekly at[data.shipbob.com](https://data.shipbob.com/) , which is an unusual level of transparency for fulfillment providers.


#### Why analytics data matters for store owners


- Cost and speed data you can act on, per order and per SKU
- Inventory visibility across every location in real time
- Exportable reporting for finance, planning, and reconciliation
- Fewer spreadsheets, because the numbers live in one place


**Proof:**[Stonehenge Health’s](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/stonehenge-health/) VP of Operations, Gregory Fry, ran a warehouse for 14 years, and finally found the complete transparent reporting on storage, fulfillment, inventory, and shipping at ShipBob. After partnering with ShipBob, Stonehenge Health saved $1M in just one year.


> *“The number one thing that any mid-market company evaluating fulfillment partners should consider is: What is the software platform like, and does it meet all your needs?*
>
>
> *For us, ShipBob absolutely met all our needs and more. They provided way more data, visibility, and ease of use than we were getting before, even more than we thought we needed. ShipBob’s already built out so many of the tools and reporting capabilities brands want, so don’t bother reinventing the wheel. You can use what ShipBob provides, because it’s all great and all right there for you.”*
>
>
> *Gregory Frye, VP of Operations at Hi-Altitude Brands*


### The AI completes actions (it doesn’t just describe)


Most AI tools in fulfillment are read-only: you ask a question, you get an answer, and you still do the work somewhere else.


ShipBob’s AI works differently, both inside your own tools and inside the dashboard.[ShipBob MCP](https://developer.shipbob.com/mcp-server/overview) brings ShipBob into the AI tools you already use, reading and writing across your fulfillment data, so you can pull up an order and reroute it in one step. The Anthropic-verified connector is live in the Claude directory, and connecting takes a few clicks.


Inside the dashboard, Bobby is an AI agent (in beta, waitlist open now) that acts on your account. Ask Bobby about an order, then have Bobby edit or create that order. Ask about your inventory, then have Bobby build a warehouse receiving order right there in the chat.


Underneath both, the fulfillment engine handles inventory placement, order routing, carrier selection, and delivery promises, while the transportation network engine handles middle- and last-mile optimization, zone skipping, and delivery estimate accuracy. This AI layer is the newest part of the platform, and it works because ShipBob owns everything beneath it.


As of writing, that engine runs at 97.6% delivery estimate accuracy while AI-powered inventory placement keeps roughly 55% of orders in-region.


#### Why actionable AI matters for store owners


- Work happens where the answer does, with no context-switching
- Exceptions get resolved in the moment, not queued for later
- Routine tasks like order edits and receiving orders move faster
- The AI tools you already use can act on real fulfillment data


**Proof:** Noah Rosenstock, Director of Operations at Chamberlain Coffee, said ShipBob’s MCP “makes it easy to turn operational data into action. We can quickly surface exceptions, understand what’s happening across orders, and resolve issues immediately through Claude or ShipBob.”


Mike McPhail, Sr. Director of Distribution at Vuori, described the effect on prioritization: “I can’t even remember the last time I was on a call where someone asked me to decide which orders to prioritize. ShipBob’s AI just fulfills what needs to come out first.”


### You keep control, and a complete record


Handing off fulfillment doesn’t mean giving up control. ShipBob’s AI is built to keep you in charge: Bobby confirms before it makes any change, logs every action, and keeps changes reversible, so you set the guardrails. The AI Hub’s MCP Insights tab gives you a live, complete view of every action AI has taken on your account, by any user or tool, Bobby included.


For inventory, you can review and override the distribution the Inventory Placement Program recommends whenever your plan calls for something different.


The result is more automation and more visibility at the same time, which is usually the trade-off store owners expect to make and don’t get:


- A complete, auditable log of every automated action
- Confirmation before changes, with the option to reverse them
- Manual overrides for when your judgment should win
- Control whether you outsource, run your own warehouse, or do both


**Proof:**[Pit Viper](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/pit-viper/) runs a hybrid setup: its own warehouse on ShipBob WMS, plus outsourced fulfillment in Canada and Australia, all visible in one system. The control showed up in the numbers. As Operations Manager Jourdan Davis explained, order accuracy went from about 92% before ShipBob WMS to 99.7% after, which worked out to roughly 2,100 fewer mispicks a year.


> *“ShipBob’s system for picking orders has cut down on labor costs, reduced lost inventory, and eliminated the need for double shipping. That’s been huge for us.*
>
>
> *Our order picking and routing has also greatly improved with ShipBob. With ShipBob’s WMS, we can create the most efficient routes through the warehouse, which has cut down on an insane amount of time and made picking, packing, and shipping so much more efficient.”*
>
>
> *Jourdan Davis, Operations Manager at Pit Viper*


## Where to go from here


If you’re evaluating fulfillment technology, ask for more than a demo. Ask what happens when you tell the system to do something, and whether it can change an operational outcome rather than just describe one.


The clearest way to see how the stack fits your operation is to look at the parts most relevant to you: the[ShipBob WMS](https://www.shipbob.com/product/wms/) if you run your own warehouse, the[AI tools](https://www.shipbob.com/product/ai/) if you want your team and your own software to act on live data, and the case studies above if you want to see the results in context.

## ShipBob’s technology FAQs


Here are answers to some of the most common questions about SHipBob’s technology.


#### Does ShipBob own its technology?


Yes. ShipBob built and owns the full stack, including the ShipBob WMS, the fulfillment engine, the transportation network engine, the merchant application, and the API layer, all on one codebase.


That ownership is what lets the platform operate as one connected system rather than a set of separate tools.


#### What analytics do store owners get?


The ShipBob dashboard provides real-time inventory across locations, SKU velocity and estimated days of inventory left, average fulfillment cost per order, storage cost per unit, shipping-method performance, and Fulfillment SLA and exceptions reporting. Reports export to CSV, and ShipBob publishes its own network performance publicly and updates it weekly.


#### Can I connect my own AI tools?


Yes. ShipBob MCP lets the AI tools you already use read and write across your fulfillment data, so you can move from insight to action in one step. The Anthropic-verified connector is live in the Claude directory, and it connects in a few clicks.


#### What is Bobby?


Bobby is ShipBob’s AI agent inside the dashboard. It can edit and create orders, build warehouse receiving orders, and resolve exceptions from a chat, and it confirms before every change, logs each action, and keeps changes reversible. Bobby is in beta, with the waitlist open now.


#### How much control and visibility do I have over my orders?


You stay in control. Bobby asks for confirmation before acting and keeps changes reversible, the AI Hub’s MCP Insights tab records every action AI takes on your account, and you can override automated inventory distribution when you need to. Whether you outsource, run your own warehouse on ShipBob WMS, or do both, you manage everything from one dashboard.
